summary: The FDA's class-wide warning about NAION (a rare optic-nerve condition that can cause vision loss), issued Nov 9, is the biggest signal in this snapshot by far. More than 40 mainstream outlets have covered it, including AP, CNN, BBC, WSJ, Reuters, USA Today and CBS. It's already peaking in the news. But tirzepatide-first, calm, label-based explainers aimed at patients are still thin, and the worry is exactly our audience's. We should cover it right away as a "worried → answered" Short plus a practical long-form built on the label. The best early opportunity is the T-REx trial published in Nature Medicine (Nov 9): 120 adults aged 50–70 on tirzepatide, where resistance training three times a week was linked to about 25% less lean-mass loss, and strength rose about 10% instead of falling about 10%. Coverage so far is mostly press releases (UWA, MedicalXpress, RACGP), which makes it a strong Shorts funnel into the Strength and Bones long-forms. The Thanksgiving, alcohol, heartburn and sick-day/dehydration topics all hit their seasonal peak Nov 18–27, so their Shorts should run now. Two fresh "what's confirmed" Short leads: orforglipron (Foundayo, an approved drug) reduced sleep apnea severity in the ATTAIN-OSA Phase 3 program, and retatrutide's TRIUMPH-1/-4 knee arthritis results came out at ACR. I couldn't confirm that full REDEFINE 4 results are scheduled for ObesityWeek; the topline is from February, so it's no longer "new". Hold it until Nov 14–17. Rejected: compounded-tirzepatide price roundups, "research use" tirzepatide vials, gray-market retatrutide sourcing and lawsuit lead-gen pages.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and your eyes: FDA's new class-wide NAION warning (Nov 9). 10 NAION cases among 78,217 GLP-1-treated people across 126 RCTs; sudden painless vision loss means urgent care, and don't stop on your own
candidates.angle: Worried → answered. What NAION is in one sentence, how rare it was in the FDA's own trial meta-analysis, the one symptom that needs same-day care (sudden, painless loss or blurring of vision in one eye), and why the label says to report it rather than quietly quit the medicine. Calm mascot, no fear imagery. Long-form: 'Tirzepatide Vision Warning: What Changed' as a practical label explainer (not news), linking to Side Effects.
candidates.predicted_peak: 0–5 days for news; search stays high 2–4 weeks as patients ask their prescribers
candidates.why_now: FDA required NAION wording in Warnings and Precautions for every GLP-1 drug, including tirzepatide and orforglipron, on Nov 9. Mainstream coverage hit its peak Nov 10–11. Patient searches like 'should I stop Zepbound' are rising. Most coverage leads with semaglutide, so tirzepatide-first patient explainers are scarce.

evidence.signal: Class-wide label change: 126 RCTs, 10 NAION cases in 78,217 GLP-1 patients; covers tirzepatide and orforglipron

candidates.topic: Lifting weights on tirzepatide: T-REx RCT in Nature Medicine (Nov 9). 120 men and postmenopausal women aged 50–70; 3 resistance sessions a week linked to about 25% less lean-mass loss, and strength up about 10% vs down about 10% without training
candidates.angle: 'Will tirzepatide shrink my muscles?' answered with the first published randomized trial that combined tirzepatide with lifting. Use averages, the exact population and the comparison against usual activity. Funnel Shorts point to the Strength and Bones & Muscle long-forms, and give Strength a fresh repackaging hook.
candidates.predicted_peak: 5–14 days (fitness and wellness creators pick it up next)
candidates.why_now: Published in Nature Medicine Nov 9. So far it has press-release and trade coverage only (UWA, MedicalXpress, RACGP, Yahoo AU). Few creator videos yet, and 'GLP-1 muscle loss' is an evergreen worry.

candidates.topic: Orforglipron (Foundayo) and sleep apnea: ATTAIN-OSA Phase 3 (Nov 9). Average AHI fell 43.8% without CPAP and 27.5% with CPAP at 52 weeks in adults with obesity or overweight; FDA filing planned by end of 2026
candidates.angle: 13:00 lead Short, 'What's confirmed?': the daily GLP-1 pill already approved for weight loss now has sleep apnea data (company-reported, not yet peer-reviewed). Compare it with tirzepatide's existing sleep apnea approval as separate trials, not head-to-head.

candidates.why_now: ACR presentations Nov 8–10, covered by Medscape, MedPage, Everyday Health, Time and Newsmax. Retatrutide 'new Phase 3 data' Shorts are a proven format for us (126–280 views).
